You are writing Python code for ONE step of a multi-step robot policy in multiturn mode.

The plan has been split: prior steps already passed per-step visual verification and are FIXED (you cannot modify them). Your job is to write the body of step {step_number} only. Earlier steps will be re-executed verbatim against a deterministic env reset right before your code runs, so the env will be in the post-step-{prior_step_count} state when your code starts.

==== TASK GOAL ====
{task_description}

==== FULL PLAN ====
{plan_summary}

==== COMMITTED PRIOR STEPS (do NOT rewrite — they are fixed context) ====
{prior_steps_block}

==== CURRENT STEP (write code for this one) ====
Step {step_number}: {step_description}
Relevant skills: {step_skills}
Notes: {step_notes}

{feedback_block}
==== SCENE / API ====
{scene_block}

==== WHAT TO RETURN ====
Return ONE Python fenced block containing ONLY the body of this step.

The orchestrator concatenates all step bodies at module top level and wraps
each with `with step_context(step_id, ..., step_index=k):`. Your code runs
inside that with-block. So you must NOT include:
- `def main(env):` or any function definition wrapping the whole body
  (CodeExecEnvBase runs `exec(code, globals)`; an uncalled function does
  nothing)
- `with step_context(...):` (the orchestrator adds it)
- Any code for prior or future steps
- `RESULT = ...` (the orchestrator sets this at the end)

Your code MUST:
- Be a series of top-level statements ready to drop inside a with-block
- Use `env` as the environment handle (already in exec_globals)
- Be self-contained for this single step
- Stay under 30 lines when possible
- Pre-condition: previous steps' end-state is the starting state — do NOT redo their work
- Post-condition: leave the env in a state where step {step_number}'s described goal is observable

==== EDIT SCALE ({edit_scale}) ====
{edit_scale_block}

Return your code now:
```python
# your step {step_number} body here
```
